issues.legal_issue: Joint ownership, common agricultural management, and distribution of profits according to ownership shares do not by themselves establish a partnership without evidence of an agreement to partner or of agency between the owners.
material_facts: Two owners jointly held agricultural land and cultivated it through a manager they appointed together.
The owners lived far from the land, and the manager supervised cultivation and managed the agricultural properties.
The land was not divided between the owners, and the manager distributed the profits according to their respective ownership shares.
The record contained no evidence of an agreement to form a partnership or that either owner acted as the other's agent.
The tax returns described the concern as co-ownership, while the printed return form had no co-ownership option and retained the word “firm.”
issues.conclusion: The concern was a co-ownership concern, not a partnership firm; the facts relied on by the tax authorities did not justify inferring a partnership.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(k) of the Bihar Agricultural Income-tax Act, “firm” has the meaning given by the Indian Partnership Act, 1932. Section 4 of that Act defines partnership as the relation between persons who have agreed to share the profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all. Co-ownership does not necessarily result from agreement or involve community of profit or loss, and one co-owner is not, merely by being a co-owner, the agent of another; partnership requires the relevant agreement and agency relationship. Common management and profit distribution in accordance with ownership shares are not alone sufficient to establish partnership. The Court also applied the principle in Modern Rigg & Co. and R. B. Eskrigge & Co. v. Monks that a finding on fact is not conclusive where the fact-finder applied an incorrect legal principle.

predicates.agricultural_income_tax_assessment: A taxing authority assesses income derived from agricultural land.
predicates.joint_owners_hold_agricultural_land: Two or more persons jointly own or hold the agricultural land from which the income is derived.
predicates.owners_jointly_appoint_manager: The owners together appoint a manager to manage or supervise cultivation of the land.
predicates.profits_distributed_by_ownership_shares: The income or profits from the land are distributed among the owners according to their respective ownership shares.
predicates.partnership_agreement_evident: The record contains evidence that the owners agreed to form a partnership.
predicates.mutual_agency_evident: The record contains evidence that one owner acted, expressly or impliedly, as agent for the others.

issues.definition: When an agricultural income tax assessment concerns jointly held agricultural land managed by a jointly appointed manager, distribution of profits by ownership shares does not make the arrangement a partnership if the record shows neither an agreement to partner nor mutual agency.

issues.legal_issue: A common manager holding agricultural land on behalf of co-owners jointly interested in the land or its income is assessable for the aggregate tax payable by the owners on their respective shares.
material_facts: The owners jointly held agricultural land and appointed a common manager to supervise cultivation and manage the agricultural properties.
The common manager managed the agricultural operations, and the resulting profits were distributed to the owners according to their respective shares.
The concern was a co-ownership arrangement rather than a partnership.
issues.conclusion: The common manager was assessable under section 13 in respect of the aggregate agricultural income tax payable by the co-owners on their respective shares.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13 of the Bihar Agricultural Income-tax Act applies where a common manager appointed under law or agreement holds land from which agricultural income is derived on behalf of persons jointly interested in the land or its income. The aggregate of the tax payable by each such person on the income derived from the land and received by that person is assessed on the manager, who is deemed the assessee for that tax and is liable to pay it. The State conceded that section 13 applied if the concern was co-ownership; the assessee conceded that the section did not apply if the concern was a partnership.

predicates.concern_is_co_ownership: The land or the income from it is held jointly by co-owners rather than through a partnership.
predicates.manager_holds_land_for_jointly_intereste: A manager appointed under law or agreement holds or manages the land on behalf of persons jointly interested in it or its agricultural income.

issues.definition: If an agricultural income tax assessment concerns co-owners who receive income from land held or managed for them by a common manager, the manager is assessed for the aggregate tax payable by those owners.

issues.legal_issue: Whether an arrangement is a partnership is ordinarily a question of fact but becomes a mixed question of fact and law when the fact-finder applies an incorrect legal test.
material_facts: The tax authorities and the High Court treated common appointment of a manager and distribution of profits according to the owners’ shares as grounds for inferring partnership.
The Supreme Court examined whether those facts supported that inference under the legal requirements of partnership, including agreement and agency.
The case reached the Supreme Court by appeals following a tax reference concerning the assessment of agricultural income.
issues.conclusion: The inference of partnership was not conclusive because the facts had been assessed using an incorrect legal approach; the facts did not establish a partnership under the proper test.
issues.legal_principle: The existence of a partnership is ordinarily a question of fact, but it is a mixed question of fact and law where the authorities apply a wrong principle in deciding what facts must be found. In that circumstance, their factual finding is not conclusive. The Court relied on Modern Rigg & Co. and R. B. Eskrigge & Co. v. Monks.

predicates.appeal_from_tax_reference: The matter comes before the court by appeal following a reference concerning a tax assessment.
predicates.partnership_inference_under_review: The court is asked to review an inference that an arrangement constitutes a partnership.
predicates.fact_finder_applied_incorrect_partnershi: The fact-finder relied on a legally insufficient test for deciding whether the arrangement was a partnership.

issues.definition: In an appeal following a tax reference, a partnership finding under review is not conclusive when the fact-finder applied an incorrect legal test.
